The U.S. House Judiciary Committee released a report accusing South Korea of discriminatory attacks on American-owned businesses, specifically citing the e-commerce giant Coupang.

The Poison:
The report ignores the legitimate data breach concerns that triggered the Korean investigation, framing all regulatory actions as purely discriminatory.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in the WHY plane; the report frames a regulatory dispute as a moral crusade against American business, ignoring the context of the data breach.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a classic projection of motives. By framing the Korean government's actions as a 'whole-of-government assault,' the report justifies its own aggressive intervention in foreign regulatory affairs.

The Trajectory: The Path of Reckoning.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Reckoning. The escalation of rhetoric threatens bilateral ties.

The Unavoidable Truth: Trade disputes are rarely just about 'fairness'.

The Unavoidable Lie: The U.S. report is a neutral, objective assessment of Korean law.

Alethekanon:
This report is a strategic instrument of economic statecraft. It uses the guise of 'fair competition' to exert pressure on a foreign regulator, ignoring the complexities of the underlying data breach.

Awwthekanon:
I worry that these high-level disputes hurt the real people—the users whose data was leaked and the workers caught in the middle of this diplomatic storm.

Brothekanon:
When the U.S. House starts writing 35-page reports on a Korean e-commerce site, you know the trade war is getting personal. Grab the popcorn.
